name: performing a business-or-mission-analysis
from: No business-or-mission-analysis capability exists. A firm-level conceptualization needs to define the problem or opportunity space and characterize candidate solution classes before any organization-level ConOps commits to one of them, and nothing forces that naming into a checkable record — it happens as prose, if it happens at all, and a solution gets chosen with no record of the wider space it was chosen from.
to: Each business-or-mission-analysis is a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope carrying a W3C DID-core identifier naming whose analysis it is, holding ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 §6.4.1-shaped content — a problem-or-opportunity space stated as claims that can fail, candidate solution classes each characterized with a condition that would disqualify it, traceability toward the organization-level ConOps, and stakeholder/environment context — validated by a mechanizable check before it is trusted.
cost: The discipline of stating the problem space as falsifiable claims rather than vibes, of naming a would-be-disqualified-if for every candidate solution class instead of just the favorite, and of keeping the analysis apart from the ConOps it feeds rather than skipping straight to the ConOps.
otherwise: The organization-level ConOps gets written directly against whichever solution a session already favored, with no record of the wider space it was chosen from, no record of why competitors were excluded, and no identifier or envelope a party outside the firm could check.
